info.name: IDRegister
info.summary: Self-registration from a phone with a photo of the identity card and a verified e-mail address
Înregistrare de pe telefon, cu poza cărții de identitate și adresă de e-mail verificată
info.description:
Visitors register themselves from their phone: they show their Romanian identity card (or driving licence) to the camera, the server reads it live (RapidOCR, with Tesseract as a fallback; MRZ, printed labels and a CNP validated by its check digit), checks that the document is physical and not a copy on a screen, and compares a selfie with the picture on the document (InsightFace, with a small head turn as the liveness proof).
In express mode the account is created right away, with a random user name and a password shown once; the e-mail address (verified with a six digit code and a link), the phone number and the nickname are added afterwards in the profile. The name taken from the document, the e-mail address and the phone number cannot be changed once set.
The picture of the document is never stored: it is read in memory and discarded. The personal number (CNP) is not stored either - only a salted hash of it, so the same card cannot be used twice. A computer cannot register: it shows a QR code and signs in after the phone is done.
Once an account exists, its owner can tie a Google account to it in their personal settings and sign in with "Continue with Google" afterwards, without a password. Google never creates an account here, and only a Google account whose Google-verified address is the address already confirmed here can be tied to one.
The same Android client can also be paired with an account: from then on the sign-in page offers "Sign in with your phone", which shows a code and two digits, and the phone - after a fingerprint - signs the answer with a key that never leaves it.
An Android client with the same flow, plus NFC reading of the chip of the electronic identity card, is at github.com/CristianCasapu/idregister-android. The document parser is a PHP port of the one in the NecMat app (github.com/CristianCasapu/necmat).
